name: status
description: Read one GitHub pull request: its state, branches, review decisions and CI checks, as JSON. With no number it finds the open pull request for the branch the workspace is on. Use to decide whether something is ready to merge, or why it is not.

number.description: The pull request number. Omit to use the open pull request whose source branch is the one the workspace is on, which fails if there is not exactly one.

repo.description: The repository as "owner/name". Omit to read it from the workspace's origin remote, which requires the workspace to be the repository root.

output_schema.description: The same field names the bitbucket pack answers with, so a flow's templates survive a change of forge. `state` is one of open, merged, closed. `mergeable` is null while GitHub is still computing it. `checks.failing` names the failing checks, so a flow can say which without a second call.

reviews.description: The latest review per reviewer. A review superseded by the same person's next one is not counted, and a plain comment is not a verdict.

checks.description: GitHub's six check conclusions mapped onto three answers: anything unfinished is pending, anything finished that did not object is success, the rest is failure.

exit_codes.0: success (the pull request is on stdout as JSON)
exit_codes.2: invalid input (a parameter is wrong, or no number was given and the branch does not identify exactly one open pull request)
exit_codes.3: not found (no such pull request or repository, or no open pull request for the branch)
exit_codes.4: not permitted (the git repository is above the workspace root)
exit_codes.5: unreachable (DNS failure, connection refused, TLS failure, or the transfer timed out)
exit_codes.6: http error (the API answered with a status that is not success, including a refused token)
exit_codes.7: no credential (GITHUB_TOKEN is not in this step's environment)
